title: Observable Neural ODEs for Identifiable Causal Forecasting in Continuous Time
claim: Under hidden confounding, latent state mediates treatment effects on outcomes, and dynamic regimes add history-dependent treatment links to the causal structure.
layout: 2 side-by-side DAG panels, left-to-right in time, green dashed arrows in (b)
description: Two side-by-side temporal causal graphs, labeled (a) and (b), each with three time points: 0, t and t+s. Every column has a disturbance node epsilon at the top, then treatment A, latent state Z and observation Y stacked below it. Black arrows run horizontally from A to A and from Z to Z. Diagonal arrows run from each A to the next Z, and vertical arrows run from Z to Y. Curved gray arrows from each epsilon go to both A and Y in the same column, which represents hidden confounding. Panel (b) repeats the same graph and adds olive-green dashed arrows. These run from each Y back to the A of the same time point, and from the early A to the late A. They show treatment depending on the observed history. The eye goes first to the green dashed arrows in (b).
caption: (a) Temporal DAG for treatment $A$, observation $Y$, and latent state $Z$ at three consecutive time points. The temporally independent latent disturbances $\epsilon$ jointly affect contemporaneous treatment assignment and observations. (b) Under a dynamic treatment regime, treatment additionally depends on the observed treatment-outcome history, as indicated by the green dashed arrows.
abstract: Causal inference in continuous-time sequential decision problems is challenged by hidden confounding and partially observed states. We show that, under explicit structural assumptions, observability of the latent state enables identification of dynamic treatment effects through a continuous-time conditional front-door adjustment, even in the presence of hidden confounding. We derive a general adjustment formula and show that it reduces to a tractable state-space formula when unobserved contemporaneous disturbances are temporally uncorrelated. This formula expresses potential-outcome distributions under alternative treatment trajectories through the measurement model, latent dynamics, and the filtering distribution over latent states. We propose Observable Neural ODEs (ObsNODEs), Neural ODE models in observable normal form that implement this tractable adjustment for causal forecasting. ObsNODEs learn continuous-time dynamics with states reconstructible from observations, enabling outcome prediction under alternative treatment paths. Experiments on synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world clinical data demonstrate strong performance over recent sequence models, including external validation.
